title: Reverse WAL group-commit stall: commit_delay 100->0, commit_siblings 2->20, wal_writer_flush_after 0->256

anomaly.source: pg_stat_activity wait events sampled by telemetry

configuration_cause: Incumbent commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a fixed group-commit sleep on nearly every commit (only 2 siblings needed with 5 terminals), adding per-commit stall without coalescing real groups; wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer-side flush batching so WAL writes are not coalesced. wal_wait persists (p95=1) and InsertTweet p95=570us.
mechanism: The r012 refutation was on predicate-lock granularity, not the WAL commit path; the WAL bundle remains the diagnosed mechanism (wal_wait alert, sync_average_ms=0.111, write_average_ms=0.020). Prior WAL attempts (r005/r006/r007/r008/r010) all widened commit_delay upward and were refuted or inconclusive, so the direction is reversed: commit_delay=0 removes the fixed per-commit sleep entirely, commit_siblings=20 (above the 5-terminal count) guarantees the zero window never activates, and wal_writer_flush_after=256 (2MB) engages writer-side flush batching so background WAL writes coalesce instead of flushing per write. This is a larger safe amplitude than r009/r011 (which used 64/128) on the flush-batch axis while fully eliminating the stall.
query_effect: InsertTweet commits no longer pay a fixed 100us group-commit sleep; writer-side flush batching coalesces WAL writes, reducing commit-path queueing for the write path while leaving the read-dominant GetUserTweets path unchanged.
expected_tps_effect: Small increase in successful_transaction_tps (>=0.3%) as commit-path stall is removed; write transactions are ~2.5% of terminal capacity so the ceiling is modest.
expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 decreases; GetUserTweets latency unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Removing the fixed 100us commit_delay sleep and enabling 2MB writer flush batching should cut InsertTweet commit-path tail.
Eliminating the group-commit stall and batching writer flushes should reduce WAL wait backends at p95.
Freed commit-path capacity raises completed transaction goodput.

alternatives.statement: If the WAL wait is fsync-bound rather than group-commit-stall-bound, sync_average_ms stays flat and TPS is unchanged; then the next lever is wal_sync_method or checkpoint cadence, not commit_delay.
If the dominant bottleneck is GetUserTweets terminal saturation (87.6% of terminal capacity) and not the write path, TPS stays flat despite lower InsertTweet latency.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent pays a fixed 100us group-commit sleep on nearly every commit (commit_siblings=2 with 5 terminals) and disables writer flush batching (wal_writer_flush_after=0). Setting commit_delay=0 with commit_siblings=20 removes the stall entirely and wal_writer_flush_after=256 coalesces background WAL writes, targeting the persistent wal_wait alert without touching the read path.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe low bound 0 (allowed [0,1000]); reverses the refuted upward direction (r005/r006/r007/r008/r010 widened to 200-500us) with the maximal safe downward amplitude, eliminating the fixed per-commit sleep.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit collection window; 0 disables the fixed sleep

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Safe high bound 20 (allowed [0,20]); with 5 terminals, 20 siblings guarantees the (zero) window never activates, preventing accidental stall.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: group-commit activation threshold; high value keeps window inactive

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Set from 0 to 256 (8kB units = 2MB) within safe [0,1024]; larger than r009/r011 (64/128) to test a larger safe amplitude of writer-side flush batching.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: writer flush batch size; batches background WAL writes

nodes.label: Remove fixed per-commit stall; engage writer-side flush batching

cross_domain_requirements: If TPS is flat while InsertTweet latency drops, the read-dominant GetUserTweets path (87.6% terminal capacity) is the binding constraint and query_execution should own the next action.
